newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Only two pct of Brazilians find Congress honest.
newsitem.headline: Only two pct of Brazilians find Congress honest.

text.p: Only two precent of Brazilians consider their legislature honest and efficient, according to an opinion poll published in the Estado de Sao Paulo newspaper on Sunday.
The survey of 400 people in Sao Paulo showed a few more believed in the honesty of the executive power -- three percent, Estado said.
"The lack of faith in the institutions is very negative for a democracy that has not yet been fully consolidated," Sao Paulo University political scientist Maria Victoria Benevides told the paper.
Though all branches of government fared dismally in the evaluation of their honesty, speed, credibility, efficiency and transparency, Congress came out worst.

Fifty-one percent of those questioned gave the legislature minimum points for honesty and speed. Thirty-nine percent said it had no credibility, 52 percent said it lacked transparency and 37 percent said it was not efficient.

The executive did only slightly better. Thirty-one percent of those polled panned its credibility, 53 percent doubted its honesty, 55 percent considered the government untransparent and 54 percent thought it moved at a snail's pace. Twenty-seven percent thought the executive efficient.

The judiciary came out of the poll best. Nine percent believed courts to be honest while only 23 percent did not. The judiciary's credibility, however, was given full marks by only 20 percent, while only two percent believed the courts acted with speed.
In terms of efficiency and transparency, the courts were given black marks by 23 percent and 31 percent respectively.

Political scientist Bolivar Lamounier told Estado he believed the survey results reflected a trend in Latin American, where populations recently freed from the yoke of military rules remained suspicious of government.
